cues.zh: 人权在今天拥有的地位，就像中世纪君权神授拥有的地位一样。
cues.en: Human rights today have the kind of status that the divine right of kings had in the Middle Ages.

cues.zh: 它们深深植根于我们的政治思维中，
cues.en: They are so deeply ingrained in our political thinking,

cues.zh: 以至于想象一个没有它们的社会几乎不可能。
cues.en: that imagining a society without them seems almost impossible.

cues.zh: 我们都知道《独立宣言》中的那句名言：
cues.en: We all know the famous line from the Declaration of Independence:

cues.zh: “我们认为这些真理是不言而喻的：人人生而平等，
cues.en: "We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal,

cues.zh: 他们被造物主赋予某些不可剥夺的权利，”
cues.en: that they are endowed by their creator with certain unalienable rights,"

cues.zh: 但我们应该警惕那些看似不言而喻的东西。
cues.en: But we should beware of what seems self-evident.

cues.zh: 在许多情况下，看似不言而喻的东西，与其说是正确或毋庸置疑的标志，
cues.en: In many cases, what seems self-evident is less an indication of what is correct or indubitable,

cues.zh: 不如说是我们偏见的标志，是我们所处时代和地点的产物。
cues.en: and more an indication of our biases, an effect of the time and place we live in.

cues.zh: 20世纪最有影响力的自由主义政治哲学家之一约翰·罗尔斯甚至说过：
cues.en: One of the most influential liberal political philosophers of the 20th century, John Rawls, once even stated that:

cues.zh: “人权不是某种特定哲学的产物，
cues.en: "Human rights are not the consequence of a particular philosophy,

cues.zh: 也不是众多世界观中某一种的产物。
cues.en: nor of one way among others of looking at the world.

cues.zh: 它们并非只与西方的文化传统绑定，
cues.en: They are not tied to the cultural tradition of the West alone,

cues.zh: 尽管这些理念最早是在这一传统中形成的。
cues.en: even if it was within this tradition that they were formulated for the first time.

cues.zh: 它们只是从正义的定义中推导出来。”
cues.en: They just follow from the definition of justice."

cues.zh: 人权“只是从正义的定义中推导出来”这一说法，至少可以说很奇怪，
cues.en: That human rights "simply follow from the definition of justice" is, at the very least, a strange claim,

cues.zh: 因为“正义”这一概念至少自古希腊人以来就已被理论化。
cues.en: because the notion of "justice" has been theorized at least since the ancient Greeks.

cues.zh: 而人权学说直到17世纪才被完整地阐述。
cues.en: Whereas the doctrine of human rights was not fully formulated until the 17th century.

cues.zh: 我们真的能把正义的定义与这一术语历史中的绝大多数内容割裂开来吗？
cues.en: Can we really untie the definition of justice from the vast majority of the terms' history?

cues.zh: 每当我们觉得某种概念或观念不可或缺时，有一种疗法我们可以使用。
cues.en: Whenever we feel like some notion or idea is impossible to do without, there is a kind of therapy we can utilize.

cues.zh: 它叫历史。
cues.en: It's called history.

cues.zh: 通过观察人权观念是如何出现的，
cues.en: By seeing how the idea of human rights emerged,

cues.zh: 我们就能把它定位为特定时间和地点的产物。
cues.en: we can then situate it as a product of a particular time and place.

cues.zh: 希望这些能消除它对政治想象力的限制。
cues.en: And those hopefully remove the limits that it places on our political imagination.

cues.zh: 开始之前，先做一个关键区分：
cues.en: A crucial distinction is in order before we begin:

cues.zh: 客观权利与主观权利之间的区分。
cues.en: the distinction between objective rights and subjective rights.

cues.zh: 客观权利规定的是普遍意义上的“正当”。
cues.en: Objective rights state what is right in general.

cues.zh: 例如，“安葬死者是正当的”，“听从父母是正当的”，
cues.en: For example, "It is right to bury the dead," "It is right to obey your parents,"

cues.zh: 或者“服务社区是正当的”。
cues.en: or "It is right to serve your community."

cues.zh: 注意，这些并没有把权利归于个人。
cues.en: Notice that these do not attribute rights to an individual.

cues.zh: 它们没有说明安葬死者是谁的权利。
cues.en: They do not state whose right it is to bury the dead.

cues.zh: 只说明这样做是正当的。
cues.en: Merely that it is right.

cues.zh: 而主观权利，则是归于个人、即主体的权利。
cues.en: Subjective rights, on the other hand, are rights that are attributed to an individual, a subject.

cues.zh: 所以叫“主观”。
cues.en: Hence, subjective.

cues.zh: 例子包括《独立宣言》中那些耳熟能详的权利。
cues.en: Examples would include the familiar rights from the Declaration of Independence.

cues.zh: “我有自由的权利”，
cues.en: "I have the right to liberty,"

cues.zh: “我有财产的权利”，“我有获得公正审判的权利”。
cues.en: "I have the right to property," "I have the right to a fair trial."

cues.zh: 这些说法并没有普遍地说明什么是正确的，
cues.en: These do not state what is right generally,

cues.zh: 而是把权利说成某人所拥有的东西。
cues.en: but rather speak of rights as something that someone possesses.

cues.zh: 正是这个范畴，即主观权利，构成了我们都很熟悉的人权观念。
cues.en: And it is this category, subjective rights, that constitutes the idea of human rights that we are all so familiar with.

cues.zh: 每个人仅仅因为生而为人就拥有的东西。
cues.en: Something that each human being owns, merely by virtue of being human.

cues.zh: 今天，我们基本上把“权利”本身等同于主观权利。
cues.en: Today, we pretty much identify "rights" as such with subjective rights.

cues.zh: 如果有人谈到权利，我们多半可以认为他们说的是主观权利这一类型。
cues.en: If someone speaks of rights, more often than not we can assume they're speaking about the subjective variety.

cues.zh: 然而，它们其实是极其晚近的发明。
cues.en: Yet, they're actually an incredibly recent invention.

cues.zh: 例如，当古希腊人谈到什么是正确的、合法的或公正的，
cues.en: When, for example, ancient Greeks spoke of what is right, or lawful, or just,

cues.zh: 他们想到的是客观概念。
cues.en: they have the objective conception in mind.

cues.zh: 对他们来说，主观权利的观念大概是无法理解的。
cues.en: To them the idea of subjective right would probably be incomprehensible.

cues.zh: 事实上，“我有权……”这样的句式，
cues.en: In fact, sentences in the form of "I have the right to..." something,

cues.zh: 在古希腊语里根本没法构造出来。
cues.en: are not even possible to construct in ancient Greek.

cues.zh: 古希腊哲学家通常认为，什么是正当的、什么是合法的，
cues.en: Ancient Greek philosophers commonly saw what is right, what is lawful,

cues.zh: 是由世界本身的道德秩序所决定的。
cues.en: as being determined by the moral order of the world itself.

cues.zh: 正当并不存在于个体之中，而存在于事物的和谐秩序里。
cues.en: What is right was not to be found in individuals, but in the harmonious order of things.

cues.zh: 存在于世界各部分与个人社群之间的关系中。
cues.en: In the relationships between the different parts of the world and ones community.

cues.zh: 罗马法有一句著名的正义定义：“给予每个人应得之物”
cues.en: Roman law famously defined justice as: "giving each person what is due to him"

cues.zh: 用我们时代的眼镜去读这句话，
cues.en: Reading this through the spectacles of our times,

cues.zh: 我们可能会以为，“给予每个人应得之物”的意思是
cues.en: we might assume that what "giving each person what is due to him" means, is something like

cues.zh: “尊重每个人的个人财产权”。
cues.en: "respecting each person's individual property rights."

cues.zh: 但正如我已经提到的，主观权利这个概念在当时根本还没有被提出。
cues.en: But, as I already mentioned, the notion of a subjective right had not even been formulated at the time.

cues.zh: 一个人应得什么，不取决于他拥有的个人权利，
cues.en: What was due to a person was determined not by the individual rights they possessed,

cues.zh: 而取决于他在更大社群中的位置，以及他与社群其他成员的关系。
cues.en: but by their position in the larger community, and their relationship to the other members of the community.

cues.zh: 这种分配正义的目标是追求社会和谐，
cues.en: The point of such distributive justice was to aim at social harmony,

cues.zh: 这只能从社群整体的角度来理解，
cues.en: something that can only be understood in light of the community as a whole,

cues.zh: 而不是从孤立的个人权利角度来理解。
cues.en: rather than in terms of isolated individual rights.

cues.zh: 那么，是什么改变了这种与我们时代常见的正义观如此不同的正义观？
cues.en: So what changed this brand of justice, so different from the one common in our times?

cues.zh: 是什么让把权利视为“主观的”成为可能？
cues.en: What made it possible to think of rights as "subjective"?

cues.zh: 就像“西方”历史上的许多事情一样，有一样东西尤为关键。
cues.en: Like many things in the history of ""the West,"" one thing in particular is crucial.

cues.zh: 基督教。
cues.en: Christianity.

cues.zh: 首先，基督教认为每个人都有灵魂。
cues.en: First of all, Christianity conceived of each individual as having a soul.

cues.zh: 这使每个人都与上帝直接相连，
cues.en: Something which places each person in direct relationship to God,

cues.zh: 从而赋予每个人一种绝对的价值。
cues.en: and thus gives each person a kind of absolute value.

cues.zh: 因为灵魂独立于个人特质和你所属的社群而存在，
cues.en: Because the soul exists independently both from one's personal qualities and the community one belongs to,

cues.zh: 于是就有可能不把个人看作其社群的具体成员，
cues.en: it becomes possible to view individuals not as the specific members of their community,

cues.zh: 而是看作抽象的人，每个人在共享共同本质上都是平等的。
cues.en: but instead as abstract human beings, each being equal in sharing a common essence.

cues.zh: 因为灵魂既是普遍的又是永恒的，
cues.en: Because the soul is both universal and eternal,

cues.zh: 于是就可以脱离时间和空间来抽象地看待人类。
cues.en: human beings could now be viewed in abstraction from both time and space.

cues.zh: 独立于他们在社群中、或更广泛地在世界中占据的位置。
cues.en: Independently from the position they occupy in their community, or the world more generally.

cues.zh: 其次：某些基督徒，例如威廉·奥卡姆，
cues.en: Secondly: certain Christians, for example: William of Ockham,

cues.zh: 最终主张，如果道德法则内在于事物的秩序之中，那就没有给上帝留下自由。
cues.en: eventually argued that if the moral law is inherent in the order of things, it leaves no freedom for God.

cues.zh: 因为上帝也必须遵循事物的秩序。
cues.en: As God must follow the order of things as well.

cues.zh: 因此，渐渐地，道德法则不再被视为事物秩序中固有的东西，
cues.en: Because of this, gradually, the moral law came to be seen not as something inherent in the order of things,

cues.zh: 而是源自上帝意志的产物。
cues.en: but something stemming from the will of God.

cues.zh: “秩序”的重要性被“意志”的重要性所取代。
cues.en: The importance of "order" is replaced by the importance of "will".

cues.zh: 最后，由于我们是上帝创造的，是照着上帝的形象造的，
cues.en: Finally, because we are created by God, in the image of God,

cues.zh: 只需一小步，就能将上帝的意志与每个人的意志等同起来。
cues.en: it takes a small step to identify the will of God with the will of each individual.

cues.zh: 于是，结果便是一种建立在普遍抽象权利之上的道德，
cues.en: Thus, the result is a morality built on universal abstract rights,

cues.zh: 这些权利源自每个人的意志，凭借的是共同的人性本质。
cues.en: which emanate from the will of each individual, by virtue of a shared human essence.

cues.zh: 我们由此抵达了成熟完整的启蒙人权观念。
cues.en: We arrive at the full-fledged enlightenment conception of human rights.

cues.zh: 有些人可能会感到惊讶，基督教在人权发展中竟扮演了如此重要的角色。
cues.en: Some might be surprised by the significant role played by Christianity in the development of human rights.

cues.zh: 但发展人权理论的思想家们在自己的著作中已把这一点说得非常清楚。
cues.en: But this was made very clear in the writings of the theorists developing human rights themselves.

cues.zh: 例如，约翰·洛克是对《独立宣言》影响最大的哲学家之一，
cues.en: John Locke, for example, one of the main philosophical influences on the Declaration of Independence,

cues.zh: 他的权利理论始于这样一个主张：上帝拥有我们，视我们为财产，
cues.en: started his Theory of Rights from the claim that God owns us as property,

cues.zh: 因此赋予我们不可剥夺的权利。
cues.en: and therefore endows us with unalienable rights.

cues.zh: 《独立宣言》本身就阐明了这一点：
cues.en: And this is stated in the Declaration of Independence itself:

cues.zh: “人人生而平等，造物主赋予他们若干不可剥夺的权利。”
cues.en: "Humans are endowed by their creator with certain unalienable rights."

cues.zh: 与宗教的相似之处不止于此。
cues.en: The religious parallels don't end there.

cues.zh: 人权与对上帝的信仰还有一个相似点：两者都被视为不言自明的东西，
cues.en: Human rights and belief in God are also similar in that both are supposed to be something self-evident,

cues.zh: 而非通过经验可以发现的事物。
cues.en: rather than something you can discover empirically.

cues.zh: 正如如今人们声称，没有人权学说，
cues.en: And just as nowadays, people claim that without the doctrine of human rights,

cues.zh: 社会就会陷入混乱。
cues.en: society would plunge into chaos.

cues.zh: 同样，过去人们也论证说，没有对上帝的信仰，社会就会陷入混乱。
cues.en: So people used to argue that society would plunge into chaos without the belief in God.

cues.zh: 到目前为止，我主要讲的是思想，也就是基督教思想。
cues.en: So far I've mostly been talking about ideas. Namely, Christian ideas.

cues.zh: 但思想不会只在天上飘着。
cues.en: But ideas don't just float around in the heavens.

cues.zh: 要真正发挥作用，就得在物质层面、在政治和社会生活中落地生根。
cues.en: In order to be effective, they need to be established materially, in political and social life.

cues.zh: 基督教的影响是显而易见的。
cues.en: The influence of Christianity is clear.

cues.zh: 但为什么人权意识形态会被如此广泛而迅速地接受？
cues.en: But why is it that the ideology of human rights became so widely and rapidly accepted?

cues.zh: 尤其是在17世纪及以后，而基督教存在的时间比那长得多。
cues.en: Specifically in the 17th century and onwards, when Christianity had existed much longer than that.

cues.zh: 如果人权背后的思想与基督教思想密不可分，
cues.en: Well, if the ideas behind human rights are inseparable from Christian thought,

cues.zh: 那么它们的政治影响就与资本主义的兴起密不可分。
cues.en: then their political influence is inseparable from the rise of capitalism.

cues.zh: 为了让资本主义启动，
cues.en: In order for capitalism to kick off,

cues.zh: 新兴资本家必须买下一块原先公有的土地，
cues.en: the emerging capitalists had to buy a plan that was previously owned communally,

cues.zh: 那本是供住在上面的人维持生计的，再把它变成私人所有、用来牟利的土地。
cues.en: for the subsistence of the people living on it, and turn it into land owned individually for profit.

cues.zh: 这就是所谓的圈地运动，
cues.en: This was known as the enclosure movement,

cues.zh: 在此期间，许多此前在公有土地上劳作、
cues.en: during which many peasants, who had previously worked on commonly owned land,

cues.zh: 为自己消费而生产的农民，
cues.en: producing for their own consumption,

cues.zh: 被强行、且往往是暴力地驱逐出这些土地。
cues.en: were forcibly and often violently removed from said land.

cues.zh: 他们从此失去财产，被迫靠工资为生。
cues.en: And, now property-less, were forced to work for a wage.

cues.zh: 于是，那些原本把自己看作更大共同体一部分、
cues.en: Thus people who previously saw themselves as part of a larger community,

cues.zh: 为共同目标而协作的人，
cues.en: working together to accomplish shared goals,

cues.zh: 如今变成了孤立的、原子化的个体。
cues.en: now became isolated and atomized individuals.

cues.zh: 生产过程也不再对他们的共同体负责，
cues.en: And the production process no longer responsible to their community,

cues.zh: 而是对老板，即资本家个人负责。
cues.en: but to their boss, the individual capitalist.

cues.zh: 集体团结逐渐被个体竞争所取代。
cues.en: Collective solidarity was gradually replaced with individual competition.

cues.zh: 工人不再是共享共同体中的成员，
cues.en: Workers ceased being fellow members in a shared community,

cues.zh: 而成了为工资而竞争的个体。
cues.en: and became individuals competing for a wage.

cues.zh: 换句话说，他们成了在生产中联合起来的个体
cues.en: They became, in other words, individuals who got together in production

cues.zh: 去追求各自私人的个体利益。
cues.en: in the pursuit of their own private individual interests.

cues.zh: 工人追求工资，资本家追求更多资本。
cues.en: Workers pursuing a wage, and capitalists pursuing more capital.

cues.zh: 人权意识形态与这种状况相伴而生。
cues.en: The ideology of human rights went hand-in-hand with the situation.

cues.zh: 它主要把自由理解为消极自由：免于什么的自由。
cues.en: It conceived of freedom primarily as negative freedom: freedom "from".

cues.zh: 比如，免于干涉的自由。
cues.en: For example, freedom from interference.

cues.zh: 取代了人们此前在追求共同目标时所体验到的积极的集体自由。
cues.en: Replacing the positive collective freedom people experienced in pursuit of shared goals before.

cues.zh: 竞争让人们把彼此视为必须加以防范的东西，
cues.en: Competition led people to view each other as something that they must be protected from,

cues.zh: 视为不断威胁要侵犯他们“权利”的东西。
cues.en: as something that constantly threatens to infringe on their ""rights.""

cues.zh: 这也是社会契约论变得如此流行的原因。
cues.en: And this is also why social contract theory became so popular.

cues.zh: 它假定社会是通过订立契约而创建的。
cues.en: Positing that society was created through the establishment of a contract.

cues.zh: 如果人天生就是个体化、原子化的，
cues.en: If people are seen as individualized and atomized by default,

cues.zh: 只有为了追求自身利益才聚在一起，
cues.en: and get together only in pursuit of their own self-interest,

cues.zh: 那么唯一能想到的组建社会的方式就是签订契约。
cues.en: then the only conceivable way to form a society is to sign a contract.

cues.zh: 这导致了黑格尔所说的市民社会与政治国家之间的严格分离。
cues.en: This led to the strict separation between what Hegel called civil society on the one hand and the political state on the other.

cues.zh: 市民社会是市场的社会，
cues.en: Civil society is the society of the market,

cues.zh: 是私人个体独立于他人追求自身利益的社会。
cues.en: of private individuals pursuing their private interests independently of anyone else.

cues.zh: 相比之下，政治国家是人们聚在一起做出共同决策的领域。
cues.en: The political state, in contrast, is the sphere in which people get together to make common decisions.

cues.zh: 纠正市民社会领域的过度行为。
cues.en: Fixing the excesses of the civil sphere.

cues.zh: 自由社会正是由这一根本性分裂塑造的。
cues.en: Liberal society was shaped by this fundamental split.

cues.zh: 一边是私人个体，另一边是国家及其机关、法院、军队和警察力量。
cues.en: Private individuals on one side, and the state with its offices, courts, army, and police force on the other.

cues.zh: 因此，马克思写道：
cues.en: Hence, Marx writes:

cues.zh: “首先，我们注意到这样一个事实：所谓人权
cues.en: "Above all we note the fact that the so called rights of man

cues.zh: 不过是市民社会成员的权利，
cues.en: are nothing but the rights of a member of civil society

cues.zh: 也就是利己的人的权利，是脱离他人、脱离共同体的人的权利。”
cues.en: i.e. the rights of egoistic man, of man separated from other men and from the community."

cues.zh: 市民社会与政治国家的分离，将个人一分为二：
cues.en: The separation between civil society and the political state splits the individual into two:

cues.zh: 一方面是市民社会中私人的、利己的个人，
cues.en: the private, egoistic individual of civil society on the one hand,

cues.zh: 另一方面是政治的人，即政治国家的公民。
cues.en: and the political man, the citizen of the political state, on the other.

cues.zh: 这也给人权意识形态制造了一种张力，
cues.en: This also creates a tension in the ideology of human rights,

cues.zh: 因为人权本应独立于任何特定政治制度而存在，
cues.en: because they're supposed to exist independently of any particular political system,

cues.zh: 但只有当国家承认一个人为公民时，这些权利才能被赋予他。
cues.en: but can only be granted to a person if the state recognizes them as a citizen.

cues.zh: 抽象普遍的人类，始终处于张力之中，
cues.en: The abstract universal human being is in constant tension

cues.zh: 与特定政治共同体的具体公民相对立。
cues.en: with the particular citizen of a specific political community.

cues.zh: 人权将个体视为普遍而抽象的存在
cues.en: The way in which human rights view individuals as universal and abstract

cues.zh: 这也契合资本主义的生产过程。
cues.en: was also befitting the capitalist production process.

cues.zh: 因为资本家雇佣工人时
cues.en: Because when a capitalist hires workers

cues.zh: 把他们看作抽象个体，仅以其劳动力来定义。
cues.en: he views them as abstract individuals, defined only by their labor power.

cues.zh: 而由于人权意识形态主张人人在形式上权利平等，
cues.en: And because the ideology of human rights posits that rights are formally equal for everyone,

cues.zh: 它有助于掩盖真实的人之间存在的巨大而真实的权力失衡。
cues.en: it helps obscure the vast and real power imbalances that exists between real people.

cues.zh: 例如，国家宣称法院是公正的，
cues.en: For example, the state proclaims that the courts are fair,

cues.zh: 因为人人都有获得公正审判的平等权利。
cues.en: because everyone has an equal right to a fair trial.

cues.zh: 但这种平等权利掩盖了一个事实：你的审判有多“公正”，取决于你请得起什么样的律师。
cues.en: But this equal right obscures the fact that how "fair" your trial is, depends on the lawyer you can afford.

cues.zh: 平等人权的学说实际上并不能让人人平等。
cues.en: The doctrine of equal human rights does not actually make people equal.

cues.zh: 这只是允许以抽象的方式来看待他们，
cues.en: It just allows them to be viewed in abstraction,

cues.zh: 脱离一切真正使他们成为他们自身的东西。
cues.en: from everything that actually makes them the person that they are.

cues.zh: 这是人权中又一个张力所在。
cues.en: This is yet another tension found in human rights.

cues.zh: 一方面，其假定的目的是保护个体的自主性，
cues.en: On the one hand, their supposed purpose is to protect the autonomy of the individual,

cues.zh: 然而就其本质而言，它必须将人抽象地看待，
cues.en: yet by its very nature, it must view human beings in abstraction

cues.zh: 脱离一切真正使他们成为个体的东西。
cues.en: from everything that actually makes them an individual.

cues.zh: 但是，即便考虑到这一切，人权仍然可能具有净正面的价值，对吧？
cues.en: But, even given all of this, it could still be the case that human rights have a net positive value, right?

cues.zh: 我们应当小心，不要在这里犯下发生学谬误。
cues.en: We should be careful not to commit a genetic fallacy here.

cues.zh: 仅仅根据某事物的来源或产生方式来判定它是坏的。
cues.en: Judging that something is bad, solely based on where it came from or how it emerged.

cues.zh: 权利可能是有价值的，
cues.en: It could be that rights are valuable,

cues.zh: 即使它们最初被宣告是为了使新兴资本家阶级的利益正当化。
cues.en: even if they were originally declared to legitimate the interests of the emerging capitalist class.

cues.zh: 不过，我认为人权的问题
cues.en: However, I think that the problem with human rights

cues.zh: 至少就我们的理解和实施方式而言，是它固有的。
cues.en: at least as we understand and implement them, is inherent to them.

cues.zh: 要解释原因，我们得先问：它的根本问题是什么。
cues.en: To explain why we must ask what their fundamental problem is.

cues.zh: 让我们从一个在理论中常被忽视或忽略的起点开始。
cues.en: Let's begin from a starting point that is often overlooked or ignored in theory.

cues.zh: 权利的强制执行。
cues.en: The enforcement of rights.

cues.zh: 自由主义政治理论家在谈论权利或法律时，
cues.en: Liberal political theorists, when speaking of rights or laws,

cues.zh: 往往像避瘟神一样避谈其强制执行。
cues.en: often avoid speaking of their enforcement like the devil.

cues.zh: 这是因为强制执行的问题会揭示出其中的权力动态。
cues.en: This is because the issue of enforcement brings to light the power dynamics at play.

cues.zh: 谁有权力去执行？
cues.en: Who has the power to enforce?

cues.zh: 但人权要真正有效，就必须被强制执行。
cues.en: But in order for human rights to be effective, they have to be enforced.

cues.zh: 必要时甚至使用暴力。
cues.en: Violently if necessary.

cues.zh: 那么谁来执行呢？
cues.en: So who enforces them?

cues.zh: 当然是那些有权力执行的人。
cues.en: Well, those who have the power to enforce them.

cues.zh: 那些掌控法院、军队和警察力量的人。
cues.en: Those who control the courts, the military, and the police force.

cues.zh: 也就是国家。一个垄断暴力的国家。
cues.en: Namely the state. A state with the monopoly on violence.

cues.zh: 而要强制执行这些权利，他们必须比你更强大，
cues.en: And in order to enforce such rights they must be more powerful than you,

cues.zh: 并且有权做出你自己不能做的行为。
cues.en: and have the permission to commit acts that you yourself cannot.

cues.zh: 那么国家为谁服务？
cues.en: And who does the state serve?

cues.zh: 好吧，即使自由主义意识形态说它服务于整个社会，
cues.en: Well, even if liberal ideology says that it serves society as a whole,

cues.zh: 它本质上必须服务于资助它的人。
cues.en: it must by its very nature serve those who fund it.

cues.zh: 否则，它根本得不到让它存在的资本。
cues.en: Otherwise, it would not receive the capital that allows it to exist in the first place.

cues.zh: 那么主要是谁资助它？
cues.en: And who primarily funds it?

cues.zh: 富人。换句话说，统治阶级。
cues.en: The wealthy. In other words, the ruling class.

cues.zh: 它必须代表他们的利益。
cues.en: It is their interests that it must represent.

cues.zh: 一些最有影响力的人权宣言是在宫殿里签署的，这并非巧合。
cues.en: It's not a coincidence that some of the most influential human rights declarations were signed in palaces.

cues.zh: 这里立刻开始出现一种根本性的张力。
cues.en: A fundamental tension immediately begins to emerge here.

cues.zh: 从政治层面讲，人权要存在，
cues.en: In order for human rights to exist politically,

cues.zh: 就必须有一个比你强大得多的人，从一开始就赋予你这些权利。
cues.en: there must be someone vastly more powerful than you, giving you those rights in the first place.

cues.zh: 人权本应让所有人平等，
cues.en: Human rights, which are supposed to make everyone equal,

cues.zh: 却矛盾地依赖于利益竞争的群体之间根本性的权力不对等。
cues.en: paradoxically depend on a fundamental power imbalance between groups with competing interests.

cues.zh: 而如果有一个比你更强大的人赋予你权利，那他们也能把权利收回去。
cues.en: And if someone more powerful than you is giving you your rights, then they can also take them away.

cues.zh: 但若果真如此，国家又为何要授予这些权利呢？
cues.en: But if this is the case, why would the state grant those rights at all?

cues.zh: 这里，尼采在《道德谱系学》中对权利的构想很有帮助。
cues.en: Here Nietzsche's conception of rights in the Genealogy of Morals is very helpful.

cues.zh: 他写道：“我的权利——就是我权力的一部分，
cues.en: He writes: "My rights - are the part of my power

cues.zh: 这部分是他人不仅让渡给我的，而且希望我保有的。”
cues.en: which others have not merely conceded me, but which they wish me to preserve."

cues.zh: “这些他人是如何达成这一点的？首先：出于他们的精明、恐惧和谨慎，
cues.en: "How do these others arrive at that? First: through their prudence and fear and caution

cues.zh: 要么是因为他们期望从我们这里得到类似的回报，
cues.en: whether in that they expect something similar from us in return,

cues.zh: 要么是因为他们认为与我们争斗既危险又毫无意义。”
cues.en: or in that they consider that a struggle with us would be perilous or to no purpose."

cues.zh: 所以说，工人阶级在经济上和政治上都很贫困。
cues.en: So, say the working class is financially and politically impoverished.

cues.zh: 他们厌倦了这种处境，于是组织起来，形成战斗性的劳工运动，并威胁要推翻国家。
cues.en: Tired of the situation, they organize together in a militant labor movement and threaten to overthrow the state.

cues.zh: 于是国家承认工人阶级是有力量的，强大到足以构成威胁。
cues.en: The state then recognizes the working class as powerful. Powerful enough to pose a threat.

cues.zh: 正因为承认了这种力量，他们决定落实某些劳工权利。
cues.en: And because they recognize this power, they decide to implement certain labor rights.

cues.zh: 这些权利之所以被落实，并不是因为国家仁慈，
cues.en: These rights are not implemented because the state is benevolent,

cues.zh: 也不是因为它在执行某种永恒的道德法则。
cues.en: or because it's enacting some eternal moral law.

cues.zh: 而是作为两个相互竞争的有力群体之间的妥协，
cues.en: Rather, they are implementing these rights as a compromise between two competing powerful groups,

cues.zh: 希望借此安抚另一方。
cues.en: in the hope that this will appease the other party.

cues.zh: “权利就是这样起源的：被承认并得到保障的权力程度。”
cues.en: "That is how rights originate: recognized and guaranteed degrees of power."

cues.zh: 这种看待权利的方式，更植根于社会和物质现实之中。
cues.en: This way of looking at rights is more embedded in social and material reality.

cues.zh: 这有助于我们看清它们如何浮现，并非作为公正永恒的法则，而是斗争的历史产物。
cues.en: It helps us see how they emerge not as impartial eternal laws, but as the historical outcomes of struggle.

cues.zh: 尼采继续道：“如果权力关系经历任何实质性的改变，
cues.en: Nietzsche continues: "If power relationships undergo any material alteration,

cues.zh: 权利便消失，新的权利被创造出来——
cues.en: rights disappear and new ones are created -

cues.zh: 正如国家间权利不断消失与重构所证明的那样。”
cues.en: as is demonstrated in the continual disappearance and reformation of rights between nations."

cues.zh: “如果我们的权力实质性地减弱，
cues.en: "If our power is materially diminished,

cues.zh: 那些迄今保障我们权利的人的感受会发生变化：
cues.en: the feeling of those who have hitherto guaranteed our rights changes:

cues.zh: 他们会考虑是否能让我们恢复到从前享有的全部权益——
cues.en: they consider whether they can restore us to the full possession we formerly enjoyed -

cues.zh: 如果觉得无能为力，他们从此便否认我们的‘权利’。”
cues.en: if they feel unable to do so, they henceforth deny our "rights""

cues.zh: 所以继续我的例子：如果工人阶级最终变得更弱，
cues.en: So to continue my example: if the working class ends up growing weaker,

cues.zh: 先前赋予它额外权利的国家，不再认为这些权利有必要，并将其剥夺。
cues.en: the state that previously granted it additional rights, no longer sees them as necessary and take them away.

cues.zh: 有点像80年代里根和撒切尔时期新自由主义兴起时发生的情况。
cues.en: Kind of like what happened in the emergence of neoliberalism in the 80s with Reagan and Thatcher.

cues.zh: 取消此前争取到的劳工权利
cues.en: The elimination of previously won labor rights

cues.zh: 伴随着劳工运动的迅速削弱。
cues.en: corresponded to a rapid weakening of the labour movement.

cues.zh: 换句话说：人权的存在本身
cues.en: In other words: the very existence of human rights

cues.zh: 就以相互竞争的群体之间存在权力斗争为前提，
cues.en: presupposes the existence of a power struggle of competing groups,

cues.zh: 较强的群体向较弱的群体授予权利。
cues.en: with the more powerful one granting rights to the weaker one.

cues.zh: 正如《立场》杂志所写：“人有权成为照料他的主人的仆人：
cues.en: As the journal Gegenstandpunkt writes: "Man has the right to be the servant of a master that attends to him:

cues.zh: 这就是启蒙运动关于自然人权伟大观念的可悲实质。”
cues.en: that is the miserable substance of the great Enlightenment notion of the natural human right."

cues.zh: 难怪最早宣布人权的两个国家：
cues.en: It's no wonder that the first two countries to declare human rights:

cues.zh: 美国和法国，也是最后废除奴隶制的国家之一。
cues.en: The United States and France, were also some of the last countries to abolish slavery.

cues.zh: 我们在阶级之间看到的这种权力动态，也同样存在于国家之间。
cues.en: This power dynamic that we see between classes also exists between countries.

cues.zh: 就拿所谓的“人道主义干预权”来说。
cues.en: Take the so-called "right of humanitarian intervention".

cues.zh: 这东西史无前例，它主张一个国家可以入侵另一个国家，
cues.en: Something with no historical precedent, which states that one nation can invade another,

cues.zh: 目的是制止侵犯人权的行为。
cues.en: for the purpose of stopping human rights violations.

cues.zh: 谁来执行人道主义干预权呢？
cues.en: Who enforces the right of humanitarian intervention?

cues.zh: 嗯，还是那些有能力这么做的人。军事和经济上的强国。
cues.en: Well, again, those who have the power to do so. The militarily and economically powerful.

cues.zh: 这就造成了一种局面：强者可以把人道主义干预当作借口，
cues.en: This creates a situation in which the powerful can use humanitarian intervention as a pretext

cues.zh: 去入侵、破坏和剥削其他国家，就像美国对南斯拉夫、利比亚、叙利亚等所做的那样。
cues.en: to invade, destabilize, and exploit other countries, like what the U.S. did with Yugoslavia, Libya, Syria, etc.

cues.zh: 而他们自己侵犯人权的行为却不受任何人的问责。
cues.en: While themselves not being accountable to anyone for their own human rights violations.

cues.zh: 我先说清楚：
cues.en: Let me be clear here:

cues.zh: 我不是说，只要不再遵循人权教条，所有这些问题就都会解决。
cues.en: I'm not saying that all these problems will be fixed if we simply stop adhering to the doctrine of human rights.

cues.zh: 人权是一种结果。是特定社会和政治格局的症状，
cues.en: Human rights are an outcome. A symptom of a specific social and political configuration,

cues.zh: 而你要对付的不是症状，而是疾病本身。
cues.en: and you don't fight the symptom, you fight the disease.

cues.zh: 如果我们认识到人权的问题所在，
cues.en: If we recognize the problem with human rights,

cues.zh: 那我们要改变的，正是产生人权的社会和政治格局。
cues.en: it is the social and political configuration that produces them that we have to change.

cues.zh: 只要我们生活在资本主义和自由主义政治范式之下，
cues.en: So long as we live under capitalism and the liberal political paradigm,

cues.zh: 权利就是绝对必要的。
cues.en: rights are absolutely necessary.

cues.zh: 但如果我们的斗争只限于乞求国家赐予我们权利，
cues.en: But if we limit our struggles to begging for the state to grant us rights,

cues.zh: 我们就永远无法解决人权所回应的那个更根本的问题。
cues.en: we will never address the more fundamental problem that human rights are a response to.

cues.zh: 也就是构成我们社会的根本性社会与政治失衡。
cues.en: The fundamental social and political imbalances that constitutes our society.

cues.zh: 公民社会与政治国家之间的分裂，
cues.en: The split between civil society and the political states,

cues.zh: 这与经济阶级之间的分裂密不可分。
cues.en: which is inseparable from the split between economic classes.

cues.zh: 此时我们可以开始看出，人权与君权神授
cues.en: We can begin to see at this point that human rights and the divine right of kings

cues.zh: 在重要方面其实非常相似。
cues.en: are actually very similar in significant respects.

cues.zh: 两者都被少数人，即统治阶级，
cues.en: Both are utilized by a minority of the population, the ruling class,

cues.zh: 用来为其统治辩护，诉诸于某种独立于社会之外的东西。
cues.en: to justify its rule by appealing to something independent of society.

cues.zh: 某种形而上学或道德法则。
cues.en: Some metaphysical or moral law.

cues.zh: 对比一下：“当然，我们之间存在巨大的权力失衡，
cues.en: Compare: "Sure, there are vast power imbalances between us,

cues.zh: 但我们都是上帝的子民，而我们这些国王，只是在执行他的旨意。”
cues.en: but we're all subjects of God, and we, the kings, are merely carrying out his will."

cues.zh: 以及：“当然，我们之间存在巨大的权力失衡，
cues.en: And: "Sure, there are vast power imbalances between us,

cues.zh: 但我们都是权利的承载者，而我们国家，只是在执行那些权利。”
cues.en: but we're all bearers of rights, and we, the state, are merely enforcing those rights."

cues.zh: 换句话说：人权意识形态，就像君权神授的意识形态一样，
cues.en: In other words: the ideology of human rights, like the ideology of the divine right of kings,

cues.zh: 试图将一种历史上偶然的政治状况自然化。
cues.en: tries to naturalize a historically contingent political situation.

cues.zh: 将其描绘成某种必然的东西。
cues.en: Portraying it as something necessary.

cues.zh: 它包含一个本质性的矛盾。
cues.en: It involves an essential contradiction.

cues.zh: 它宣称人权是独立于国家而存在的东西，
cues.en: It declares human rights to be something that exists independently of states,

cues.zh: 尽管这样的人权本身就预设了国家的存在。
cues.en: even though such human rights inherently presuppose the existence of a state.

cues.zh: 那么，要建立一个社会，需要做些什么
cues.en: So, what would need to be done in order to establish a society

cues.zh: 一个不再产生或依赖于人权意识形态的社会？
cues.en: that no longer produces or depends on the ideology of human rights?

cues.zh: 那必须是一个共同体的意义得到恢复的社会。
cues.en: It would have to be a society in which the significance of community has been restored.

cues.zh: 一个集体决策不局限于国家，
cues.en: A society where collective decision-making is not confined to the state,

cues.zh: 而是从地方层面开始，贯穿整个社会的社会。
cues.en: but characterizes society as a whole, starting from the local level.

cues.zh: 一个社会，生产不再是追求私利的个人的事，
cues.en: A society where production is not the affair of private individuals pursuing their self-interest,

cues.zh: 而是一个社会性规划的过程。
cues.en: but a socially planned process.

cues.zh: 只有当人们重新掌握对自己生活和自身活动的权力，
cues.en: It is only when people reclaim power over their own lives and their own activities,

cues.zh: 他们才不再需要国家来赋予他们权利。
cues.en: that they no longer need a state to grant them rights.

cues.zh: 因为他们的权力从一开始就不再被国家所异化。
cues.en: Because their powers would no longer be alienated by a state in the first place.

cues.zh: 当决策不再是少数国家官员的专属任务，
cues.en: When decision-making is no longer the task of a select minority of state functionaries

cues.zh: 而成为每个相关者的任务，自由才能真正实现。
cues.en: and becomes the task of everyone concerned, only then can freedom be realized.

cues.zh: 不是原子化个体那种抽象虚假的自由，
cues.en: Not the abstract sham freedom of the atomized individual,

cues.zh: 而是只有通过与他人联合才能实现的真正自由。
cues.en: but the real freedom that can only be realized through association with others.

cues.zh: 这样的社会将消除市民社会与政治国家之间的区分，
cues.en: Such a society would have done away with the distinction between civil society and the political state,

cues.zh: 消除个体的人与抽象公民之间的区分。
cues.en: between the individual human and the abstract citizen.

cues.zh: 一如既往，没人能像马克思说得那么漂亮。
cues.en: As usual, no one puts it as beautifully as Marx.

cues.zh: “只有当现实的个人把抽象的公民复归于自身，
cues.en: "Only when the real, individual man re-absorbs in himself the abstract citizen,

cues.zh: 并且作为个人，在自己的经验生活、
cues.en: and as an individual human being has become a species-being in everyday life,

cues.zh: 自己的个体劳动、自己的个体关系中间，成为类存在物的时候，
cues.en: in his particular work, and in his particular situation,

cues.zh: 只有当人认识到自身‘固有的力量’是社会力量，
cues.en: only when man has recognized and organized his "own powers" as social powers,

cues.zh: 并把这种力量组织起来因而不再把社会力量以政治力量的形式同自身分离的时候，
cues.en: and, consequently, no longer separates social power from himself in the shape of political power,

cues.zh: 只有到了那个时候，人的解放才能完成。”
cues.en: only then will human emancipation have been accomplished."

cues.zh: 这样的社会对我们来说可能很难想象，就像农奴很难想象我们的社会一样。
cues.en: Such a society may be as hard for us to imagine as it would have been for a serf to imagine ours.

cues.zh: 但只有当我们摒弃这个时代的政治教条，才能开始设想解放。
cues.en: But it is only when we reject the political dogmas of our times that we can begin to envision emancipation.

cues.zh: 现在，让我感谢市民社会中的各位私人个体，
cues.en: And now, let me thank my private individuals of civil society

cues.zh: 你们聚集于此，只为追求自身利益。
cues.en: collected here only in pursuit of their own self-interest.

cues.zh: 还有这些，私人的、利己的个体。
cues.en: As well as all of these, private, egoistic individuals.

cues.zh: 我还要感谢为本视频朗读引文的YouTube同行们。
cues.en: I'd also like to thank the fellow YouTubers who read out quotes for this video.

cues.zh: 他们很棒，你可以在下方找到他们的信息。
cues.en: They are great and you can find their info below.

cues.zh: 这大概是我迄今最劲爆的观点了，因为我们在YouTube上要彻底激进一把。
cues.en: This has probably been my hottest take yet, because we're going full radical here on YouTube.

cues.zh: 希望你喜欢，并记住：
cues.en: I hope you enjoyed it, and remember:

cues.zh: 废除一切。谢谢。
cues.en: Abolish everything. Thank you.
